items.title: Spain's regularization process allows 1.17 million to work legally
items.body: Spain's extraordinary regularization process has admitted more than 70% of the 1.17 million applications, allowing immigrants to work and reside legally on a provisional basis. The surge in legal workers is already boosting tourism employment, helped by a rebound in autónomo (self-employed) registrations. Social Security data confirm the figures, providing a path to legal status for those already living in Spain.

items.title: Spain home sales hit best June in 19 years, rising 1.6%
items.body: Home sales in Spain rose 1.6% in June to 59,288 transactions, breaking a five-month decline and reaching the best June since 2007, according to the National Statistics Institute (INE). New home purchases jumped 6.3% to 12,766, while resales edged up 0.3% to 46,522. Year-to-date sales are down 2.6%, but regional gains were led by Navarra (+22.6%) and Castilla-La Mancha (+22.2%).

items.title: Global food prices hit highest level since January 2023
items.body: The UN Food and Agriculture Organization's (FAO) food price index rose 0.6% in July to 131.1 points, the highest since January 2023, though still 18.2% below the March 2022 peak. Cereal prices surged 3.4% month-on-month on wheat supply worries, while vegetable oils hit their highest since June 2022. Rising global costs may feed into higher grocery bills in Spain.

items.title: Ibex 35 dips 0.02% after four record highs, still up 16.7% in 2026
items.body: The Ibex 35 closed Friday at 20,176 points, snapping a streak of four record highs with a fractional loss. The dip followed US jobs data showing 23,000 positions lost in July, the worst since 2010. Despite the slip, the index gained nearly 2% for the week and is up 16.7% year-to-date.

items.title: Spain imposes temporary border checks on travelers from Italy starting today
items.body: Spain has introduced random identity checks at ports and airports for arrivals from Italy, effective from 00:00 on August 8 through September 7. The move came after Italy refused to lift its own controls on travelers from Spain, with Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni insisting on keeping restrictions. Checks will cover identity, passport, nationality and, for third-country nationals, visa or residence permit.

items.title: Spain reinforces Ceuta with 2,000 soldiers ahead of possible August 15 mass entry
items.body: The government has deployed nearly 300 riot police, 2,000 soldiers and drones to Ceuta after credible calls on social media for a mass border crossing on August 15. Groups with up to 400,000 members are circulating slogans like '15/08' and 'al-hajma'. A 500-metre maritime barrier has been built at the Tarajal jetty to prevent entry by swimming.

items.title: Spain counts 1,342 unaccompanied minors in Ceuta, prosecutor warns regions to host them
items.body: Following the mass entry of 72,000 people, the government has identified 1,342 unaccompanied minors in Ceuta and expects the number to rise. Relocation to mainland Spain should begin within weeks, but Spain's Attorney General, Teresa Peramato, has issued guidelines warning that prosecutors will act if autonomous communities refuse to accept them. A technical team will move to Ceuta on August 16.

items.title: Wildfire in Niebla, Huelva remains out of control, UME deployed
items.body: A wildfire in Niebla (Huelva) that started Thursday remains uncontrolled due to shifting winds, forcing the activation of the Military Emergencies Unit (UME). Sixty-six people have been evacuated, two roads have been closed, and 24 aircraft battled the flames on Friday. The fire's erratic behaviour has complicated containment.

items.title: Smoke from Castellón wildfire prompts confinement order in Sierra Engarcerán
items.body: Emergency services ordered residents of Sierra Engarcerán (Castellón) to stay indoors, close windows and switch off ventilation due to heavy smoke from a forest fire that started Friday in Vall d'Alba. Situation 2 of the PEIF was activated and some farmhouses were evacuated. The Es-Alert message warned that the smoke posed a health risk.

items.title: Total solar eclipse to cross northern Spain on August 12
items.body: A total solar eclipse will be visible across northern Spain on August 12, with the path entering through Galicia and reaching its maximum at around 20:28 in A Coruña. The northern part of the peninsula and the Balearic Islands are in the full-visibility zone, while southern Spain will see a partial eclipse. The IGN has an interactive map with exact local times.

items.title: Yolanda Díaz formalizes her candidacy to lead the International Labour Organization
items.body: Second Vice President Yolanda Díaz has formally presented her bid to become director of the International Labour Organization (ILO), proposing a global charter of labour rights. She warns that the ILO faces an 'existential risk' due to a financial and programmatic crisis. The current director, Gilbert F. Houngbo, is running for re-election.
